reply_text:
㊥ (completed nodes) Fair. The tree and list started from the failing rows, so the finished parts were only visible as leaves. `rowtree.py` now opens with a COMPLETE section: rows that compile and whose dependencies all compile too. There are 22. Ten of them are also checked against Lean (█):

```
█ ParserState.restore    built on SyntaxStack.shrink, Array.shrink
█ SyntaxStack.extract    built on Array.extract, Array.extract.loop
█ Array.extract          built on Array.extract.loop
█ ParserState.pushSyntax built on SyntaxStack.push
█ SyntaxStack.shrink     built on Array.shrink
█ Array.extract.loop, Array.shrink, ParserFn.run, ParserState.stackSize, SyntaxStack.push   (no row deps)
```

The other 12 compile, and so does everything they depend on, but they have no Lean expectations yet. One of them, `Syntax.isOfKind`, is built on `Syntax.getKind`. The 12 are `atEnd`, which fails its check, plus:
- `epsilonInfo`, `isTerminalCommand`, `withStackDrop`;
- `Syntax.getArg`/`getArgs`/`getKind`/`isNone`/`isOfKind`;
- `mkListNode`, `List.foldl`, `AssocList.foldlM`.

㊟ (what the section shows)
- **No compiled row sits on a failing one.** Everything that compiles has its whole dependency tree compiling, so the finished part is a set of complete subtrees at the bottom.
- **They're small.** The largest finished chain is three rows deep (`restore` → `SyntaxStack.shrink` → `Array.shrink`).
- **Next after these** come the READY rows from before. `Array.append`, `List.foldlM` and the instance-naming rows are what the next layer up waits on.

㊭ (follow-up) The 11 rows that compile without a Lean check are cheap to check: codex-6 could write their expectations, which takes no compiler work. That would turn ▓ into █ or reveal more false "ok"s like `atEnd`. Shall I give codex-6 that, and switch the repair order to `List.foldlM` → instance naming → `mkUnexpectedError`?

previous_reply_acts.text: (priority order and tree) It isn't linear, so there's now a tree. The sections don't depend on each other as wholes; individual rows do. I built the dependencies between the 110 rows from Lean's own native dependency data (the v4.29 closure), so any row's tree shows what must compile before it can. That gives a priority list: failing rows whose own dependencies already compile, ranked by how many rows wait on them.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the tree shows that the flat map hid)
- **Unassigned rows with many dependents.** `List.foldlM` (28) and the anonymous-instance-naming problem (22 + 15 + 8 dependents, one error shared by four rows) are blocking more than most of the current work.
- **`mkEOIError` is blocked by another row.** It depends on `ParserState.mkUnexpectedError`, which fails and has nobody on it. So even if codex-18's fix works, `mkEOIError` probably won't compile until `mkUnexpectedError` does.
- **Tonight's merged work sits at the bottom.** For example, `ParserState.restore` → `SyntaxStack.shrink` → `Array.shrink`, all █.

- The dependencies come from Lean's compiled code. They miss dependencies on types and macros, so the port can need more than the tree shows.
- A ░ row's error may be from the sweep before tonight's fixes.
